IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL No.     OF 2026
(@ SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CIVIL) No.14028/2024
M.SAKRAVARTHI VINAYAKA SARAVANAN ..... APPELLANT(S)
              VERSUS
THE  MANAGEMENT  TAMIL  NADU  STATE
TRANSPORT CORPORATION (KUMBAKONAM)
LIMITED & ANR.
..... RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. We have heard learned counsel for the parties.
3. Appellant has taken exception to the Order dated 29.02.2024
passed by a Division Bench of the High Court of Judicature at
Madras (briefly the ‘High Court’ hereinafter) allowing the Writ
Appeal of the respondent.
4. Appellant was a workman in the service of Tamil Nadu State
Transport Corporation (Kumbakonam) Limited. On the allegation of
misappropriation of funds, a domestic inquiry was held against the
appellant workman whereafter he was dismissed from service on
29.06.2019.
5. Approval petition No.107 of 2019 was filed by the respondent-
management before the Special Joint Labour Commissioner, Chennai,
1

## Page 284

under Section 33(2) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.
6. By  order  dated  05.03.2021,  the  Special  Joint  Labour
Commissioner rejected the approval petition as being belated.
Additionally, the Special Joint Labour Commissioner on merit also
found fault with the domestic inquiry conducted by the respondent-
management against the appellant workman whereafter it was held
that such dismissal amounted to unfair labour practice with the
intention to victimise the workman appellant.
7. Respondent-management thereafter filed a Writ Petition being
Writ Petition No.14191/2021 before a Single Bench of the High Court
assailing the illegality and correctness of the aforesaid order
dated  05.03.2021.  Learned  Single  Judge  vide the  order  dated
01.08.2021 held that there was a delay of 6 days in reaching the
authority  for  approval  request  under  Section  33(2)  of  the
Industrial Disputes Act,  1947. Therefore, learned Single Judge
held that the approval petition was rightly rejected by the Special
Joint Labour Commissioner on account of delay in forwarding the
same.
8. This order of the Learned Single Judge came to be challenged
by the respondent-management before the Division Bench in Writ
Appeal No.3077/2021. By the impugned judgment and Order dated
29.02.2024, the Division Bench held that there was no delay in
filing the approval petition before the competent authority. While
allowing the Writ Appeal, the order of the learned Single Judge
dated 01.08.2021 has been set aside. 
2

## Page 285

9. Learned counsel for the appellant workman has strenuously
argued that the Division Bench could not have arrived at the
conclusion that there was no delay in filing the approval petition
as there was no such pleading to that effect nor any document
exhibited. Only in the course of the hearing, the postal receipt
was placed before the Court. On the other hand, learned counsel for
the respondent-management submits that the view taken by the
Division Bench is correct. This point has been raised in the memo
of appeal by the respondent-appellant. 
10. We are broadly in agreement with the view taken by the
Division Bench on the question of delay in dispatching the approval
petition. Section 33(2) of the Industrial Disputes Ac, 1947 does
not prescribe any time limit for making of such application.
Ofcourse, it goes without saying that since the subject matter of
such application is in respect of conditions of service of a
workman, the same has to be made promptly. However, in the facts
and circumstances of the case, a delay of 6 days may not be fatal.
11. Though an endeavour was made by learned senior counsel for the
respondent-management to question the interference by the Special
Joint Labour Commissioner, we are of the view that when the
Division Bench took the view that there was no delay in filing the
approval petition, it ought to have remanded the matter back to the
forum of the learned Single Judge to consider the decision of the
Special Joint Labour Commissioner on merits.
12. In view thereof, while not interfering with the reasonings and
findings given by the Division Bench in paragraph 6 of the impugned
3

## Page 286

judgment and order, we remand the matter back to the learned Single
Judge for adjudication of the Writ Petition on merit. We make it
clear that we have not expressed any opinion on merits and all
contention on either side are kept open save and except the
question of delay in dispatching the approval petition. Since it is
a matter relating to a workman and the Writ Petition is of the year
2021, we would request the learned Single Judge to expedite the
hearing of the Writ Petition and in any view to dispose of the same
within a maximum period of 6 months from today.
13. It will be open to the appellant-workman to make requisite
application before the learned Single Judge under Section 17B of
the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.
14. Appeal is accordingly disposed of.
15. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.

O R D E R
Leave granted.
2. These appeals are filed against the common order in
revision by two of the revision applicants claiming parity
with another order insofar as the mesne profits granted is
concerned.
3. In the common order, we are concerned with Civil Revision
Application (CRA) No.989 of 2014 and CRA No.1010 of 2014, to
understand the facts of which, Paragraphs 4 and 5 of the
impugned order are extracted hereinunder: -
“4. Revision Applicant in CRA/989/2024 filed Mesne
Profit  Application  No.9  of  2005  against  the
Respondent  for  recovery  of  the  mesne  profit  in
respect of office No.605 admeasuring about 500 sq.
ft. on sixth floor of Maker Chamber No. IV, Nariman
Point, Mumbai 400 021. The said application was
allowed directing the Respondent to pay mesne profits
@ 12/- per sq. ft. per month from 01.01.2002 till
actual delivery of possession alongwith interest.
Revision Applicant filed Misc. Appeal No.542 of 2009
before the Appellate Bench of Small Causes Court,
1

## Page 309

which appeal was dismissed under impugned judgment
and order dated 07.05.2014.
5. Revision  Applicant  in  CRA/1010/2014  filed
Mesne Profit Application No.3 of 2005 against the
Respondent  for  recovery  of  the  mesne  profit  in
respect of office No.606 admeasuring about 500 sq.
ft. on sixth floor of Maker Chamber No. IV, Nariman
Point, Mumbai 400 021. The said application was
allowed directing the Respondent to pay mesne profits
@ 12/- per sq. ft. per month from 01.01.2002 till
actual delivery of possession alongwith interest.
Revision Applicant filed Misc. Appeal No. 535 of 2009
before the Appellate Bench of Small Causes Court,
which appeal was dismissed under impugned judgment
and order dated 07.05.2014.”
4. The applicants before the High Court claimed parity with
the mesne profits granted in  STC v. Neelam Choudhary  (CRA
No.111 of 2019 decided on 16.10.2024). However, the impugned
order found that there should be parity with STC v. Ravinder
Singh (CRA No.308 of 2011 decided on 28.11.2025). It was
pointed out that in STC v. Ravinder Singh, a rate of Rs.90 per
sq. ft. per month was granted, which was retained by this
Court in an SLP filed by the STC. The landlord therein had not
filed for enhancement, which was allowed in one another case
between STC v. Godavaridevi awarding Rs.150 per sq. ft. per
month.
5. The specific contention of the appellant herein is seen
from Paragraph 18 of the impugned order which is extracted
hereinunder: -
“18. In CRA 989/2014 and CRA/1010/2014, possession
was handed over by STC to respective Applicants on
25.04.2011. In rest of the matters, possession was
handed  over  by  STC  to  respective  Applicants  on
01.03.2011.  Therefore,  the  period  for  which  mesne
profits are awarded is from 01.01.2002 till 01.03.2011
or 25.4.2011. This Court in the judgment of STC Vs.
2

## Page 310

Ravinder Singh (supra) has considered the period from
01.10.2003 to 31.10.2010 which is a little shorter
period than the present group of petitions. In STC Vs.
Neelam Choudhary (supra), another learned Single Judge
of this Court has granted Rs.150/- per sq. ft. per for
a period between September 2003 to December 2007 and
Rs.250/- per sq. ft. per from January 2008 till August
2012.”
(underlining supplied by us for emphasis)
6. It is pointed out by Learned Counsel for the appellant
that  the  aforesaid  determination  of  mesne  profits  was
challenged by STC in Special Leave Petition (C) No.31033 of
2024, which was rejected by order dated 15.01.2025 and a review
petition filed, again by the STC, was rejected by order dated
23.09.2025.
7. We hence modify the impugned order awarding mesne profits
as  awarded  in  STC  v. Neelam  Choudhary,  emphasized  by
underlining in the above extract.
8. The appeals are allowed to the above extent.
9. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

1. Heard.
2. Delay condoned.
3. Leave granted.
4. The present appeal(s) arises out of the judgment dated 12.03.2025 passed in
CWP No.26692/2021 and review order dated 05.02.2026 passed in RA-CW-
18/2026 whereby jurisdictional High Court upheld the revised layout plan of e-
auction process relating to auction of nursing home sites in Sector 21,
Panchkula and simultaneously directed the appellant(s) herein to issue an
allotment letter and execute the conveyance deed in favour of Respondent
No.1. The dispute originated when the appellant(s) conducting an e-auction of
nursing home sites Nos.1, 2 and 3 situated in front of House No.1957, Sector 21,
Panchkula.
1

## Page 319

5. Respondent Nos.2 to 24 challenged the revised layout plan dated 25.10.2021
and sought to restraining the auction proceedings and Respondent No.1
claimed entitlement for allotment of the site which was auctioned being the
successful Bidder. According to the appellant herein, though High Court upheld
the validity of the revised layout plan and the auction process, it committed an
error by directing issuance of an allotment letter and execution of the
conveyance deed in favour of Respondent No.1 herein, despite the factual and
legal impediments pointed out by the appellants. Hence, for modifying the said
order or setting aside the said direction, the present appeal(s) has been filed.
6. We have heard the learned senior counsels appearing for the parties and
have bestowed our careful and anxious considerations to the rival contentions
raised at the Bar. It is the contention of the appellant that consequential
directions regarding allotment and execution of the conveyance deed is
contrary to the material on record and said direction could not have been issued
after upholding the revised layout plan and also the auction process. It is
contended that High Court exceeded the scope of the writ proceedings in
granting such a relief. Per contra, the learned senior counsel appearing on
behalf of Respondent No.1 would support the said direction issued by the High
Court by placing heavy reliance on the grounds urged in the review petition
itself whereunder the appellant(s) herein had not only defended the e-auction
process conducted but also Respondent No.1 having been declared as the
successful highest Bidder and as such the necessary corollary was appellant-
authority had to only issue the allotment letter and conveyance deed and it is
for this precise reason, a writ of mandamus has been issued to the authorities
and defending the same he prays for dismissal of the appeal(s).
7. As noticed hereinabove, at the time of entertaining the writ petition the High
Court had granted the stay of further proceedings pursuant to the e-auction
conducted by the appellant(s). After having upheld the revised layout plan as
well as the auction process conducted by the appellant(s) herein, the High Court
2

## Page 320

ought to have restricted to that extent only. The High Court committed a
serious error in issuing Mandamus to the appellant(s) herein to issue the
allotment letter and the conveyance deed. As a consequence of dismissal of the
writ petition by upholding the revised layout plan, the necessary steps that
ought to have followed, would have automatically followed and as such without
expressing any opinion on the contentions with regard to the rights of
Respondent No.1 to claim issuance of allotment letter and conveyance deed or
the right of the appellant(s) to either issue the letter of intent/conveyance deed
or cancel the e-auction process and leaving all such contentions open, we
modify the High Court order only to the extent of the directions that have been
issued to the appellant(s) to issue LOI/allotment letter/conveyance deed in
favour of Respondent No.1 as not warranted and setting aside the same and
maintaining the order of the High Court to the extent of dismissal of the writ
petition and upholding the revised plan and e-auction process, we allow this
appeal(s) in part to the extent aforestated above. No orders as to costs.
8. All pending application(s) stands consigned to records.

25th September,  2025  registered  with  Police  Station  Karol  Bagh,
Central  Delhi.  It  is  alleged  in  the  FIR  that  the  appellant  has
committed offences punishable under Sections 318(4), 316(2) and
3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023.

allegations, we are of the opinion that custodial interrogation of the
appellant is not necessary and that there is sufficient ground for the
appellant to be admitted to an order for grant of bail in anticipation
of arrest.

aside.

in connection with proceedings arising out of the aforesaid FIR, he

court on terms and conditions to be fixed by the trial court.
9. It is made clear that in the event the appellant breaches any of

liberty to cancel the bail of the appellant.

O R D E R 
 
 
 Leave granted. 
 
2. The plaint simplicitor for relief is extracted hereunder:- 
 
 “The plaintiff’s suit be accepted and a judgment 
and decree to the following effect be kindly granted 
against defendants No. 1 and 2:- 
 
01- That an injunction be issued in favor of the 
plaintiff and against defendants No.1 and.2, 
restraining them from interfering in any manner 
with the plaintiff’s possession of the land 
described in paragraph one of the plaint, which 
is shown in red ink in the  attached map and is 
under the legal ownership and possession of the 
plaintiff, either by themselves or through any 
other associates.  And, they shall not cause any 
obstruction or damage to the plaintiff’s use and 
enjoyment of the disputed land under the 

## Page 347

plaintiff’s possession, or to the plaintiff’s 
construction work. 
…” 
 
3. After a period of almost 4 years, the plaintiff filed an 
application under Order 6 Rule 17 CPC seeking amendment of 
the plaint to the following effect:- 
“01(a):- That it be declared that the plaintiff has 
acquired title over the purchased land by virtue of 
registered sale deed document no. 
MP452732018A1692199 dated 11 -10-2018 and 
sale deed document no.MP452732018A1692195 
dated 11-10-2018” 
 
The said application was rejected by the Trial Court vide order 
dated 6.10.2025 inter alia on the ground that the same was filed, 
(a) as an afterthought; (b) belatedly; (c) with an intent of delaying 
the proceedings ; (d)  not to be in consonance with the settled 
principles of law ; and (e) amendment would change the nature 
and character of the proceedings.  However, while reversing the 
order passed by the Trial Court, the High Court allowed the 
application vide impugned order dated 24.03.2026.   
4. Having perused the same, we are of the considered view 
that the only reason assigned by the High Court is “ crucial for 
determining the true nature of the dispute between the parties ”.  

## Page 348

Now, what is the reason for coming to such a conclusion is not so 
stated in the order.  Mere reliance on the decision rendered by this 
Court in Dinesh Goyal alias Pappu vs. Suman Agarwal (Bindal) 
and Others 1 without any discussion of applicability of the 
principles enunciated therein, to the instant facts would not fulfil 
the requirement of any reasoned order.  The Court did not even 
consider or discuss the reasons assigned by the Trial Court in 
disallowing the application.  The prejudice caused to the appellant 
is not merely procedural but substantive in nature inasmuch as a 
valuable right had accrued in his favour with the passage of time.  
A mere suit for injunction was sought to be c onverted to that of 
declaration of title and that too without exercising any due 
diligence, as is so mandated under the statute.  Hence, for all the 
aforesaid reasons, the impugned order passed by the High Court 
of Madhya Pradesh at Gwalior in Misc.Petition No.6317 of 2025 
is quashed and set aside.  The appeal is disposed of.

3. This  appeal  arises  from  an  order
dated 21.01.2026 passed by the High Court of
Judicature at Patna rejecting the regular
bail prayer of the appellant in connection
with Case No. 676/2025, registered at P.S.
Mohaniya, District Kaimur (Bhabua).
4. According  to the  prosecution case,
the victim was found on the terrace of
Ramakant’s house. Ramakant is the father of
the appellant. The victim complained to her
mother that she became unconscious because
some scented handkerchief was put on her
face by the appellant and, thereafter, she
1

## Page 359

does not remember as to what happened.
5. It is not in dispute that her medical
examination was conducted promptly and the
medical report found no injury and no signs
of recent sexual intercourse. Even to the
Doctor, she had not reported any incident of
sexual intercourse or sexual assault on her.
6. The  submission  on  behalf  of  the
appellant  is  that  he  has  been  falsely
implicated; there is no medical report to
corroborate  the  allegations  which  were
leveled as an afterthought; and they never
appeared in the First Information Report or
in the statement of the victim made to the
Doctor.  In  such  circumstances,  it  is
submitted that the appellant, who has no
previous  criminal  antecedents  and  has
suffered  incarceration  for  a  period
exceeding  one  year,  is  entitled  to  be
released on bail at this stage. 
7. The  learned  Counsel  for  the  State-
respondent has opposed the prayer for bail
but could not dispute that there was no
2

## Page 360

specific allegation of sexual assault in the
First Information Report and there is no
corroboration of the aforesaid allegation in
the medical examination report.
8. Having regard to the above, without
expressing any opinion on the merits of the
prosecution case, we are of the view that
the appellant is entitled to be released on
bail at this stage.
9. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.
The order passed by the High Court rejecting
the regular bail prayer of the appellant is
set aside.

trial court may deem fit to impose in the
facts and circumstances of the case.

imprisonment with fine. The Appeal preferred by the

appearing for the State.

error of law could be said to have been committed by the
High Court in passing the impugned Judgment and Order.
5.  However,  we  take  notice  of  the  fact  that  the
petitioner is undergoing sentence of life imprisonment
past 16 years.

the State to place on record the following:

victim;

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Our order dated 29.05.2026 reads thus:-
“1. The petitioner before us was put to trial for the
offence punishable under Section 139 of the Negotiable
Instruments Act. She was held guilty for the alleged
1

## Page 367

offence. She went in appeal before the Sessions Court.
The appeal also came to be dismissed. 
2. She is now before the High Court invoking the
revisional jurisdiction under Section 397 read with 401
of the CrPC.
3. The High Court seems to have declined to entertain
the revision application on the ground that unless and
until the petitioner surrenders, the revision cannot be
heard on merits. In such circumstances, the petitioner
is before us.
4. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner has
instructions from her client to make a statement that
the petitioner is ready and willing to deposit the
entire cheque amount, i.e., Rs.9,30,000/- (Rupees Nine
Lakh Thirty Thousand only) with the Registry of this
Court within a period of eight (08) weeks from today,
i.e., on or before 27.07.2026.
5. If the amount of Rs.9,30,000/- is deposited with the
Registry of this Court, then notice be issued to the
respondent (original complainant). Dasti service, in
addition, shall be permitted.
6. Since the petitioner has expressed her inclination to
deposit the amount, no coercive steps be taken against
her till the next date of hearing.
7. List on 13.08.2026.”
2. Today, when the matter was taken up for further
hearing, Ms. Nishita Jagetia, the learned counsel appearing
for the petitioner submitted that her client has deposited
an  amount  of  Rs.9,30,000/-  (Rupees  Nine  Lakh  Thirty
Thousand only) with the Registry of this Court.
3. Here is a case, wherein the High Court declined to
entertain  the  Revision  Application  preferred  by  the
petitioner against the concurrent findings of two Courts
2

## Page 368

below  holding  the  petitioner  guilty  of  the  offence
punishable under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments
Act. The High Court made it a condition precedent for the
petitioner and said that unless and until the petitioner
surrenders, it shall not look into the Criminal Revision
Petition preferred by the petitioner on its own merits.
4. We would like to put an end to this entire dispute
between the parties.
5. In such circumstances, we want the petitioner to
deposit Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakh only) more, with the
Registry of the High Court of Allahabad.
6. Let this additional amount of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees
Two Lakh only) be deposited with the Registry of the High
Court of Allahabad within a period of six months from
today.
7. The amount which has been deposited with the Registry
of this Court, i.e., Rs.9,30,000/- (Rupees Nine Lakh Thirty
Thousand  only)  shall  be  disbursed  in  favour  of  the
respondent-complainant  at  the  earliest,  after  due
verification.
8. Once the additional amount of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees
Two Lakh only) has been deposited by the petitioner with
the Registry of the High Court of Allahabad, the High Court
shall immediately take up the Revision Petition for hearing
and allow the same. In other words, the High Court shall
set aside the judgment and order of conviction passed by
the Trial Court, as affirmed by the Appellate Court.
3

## Page 369

9. The additional amount of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two
Lakh only) shall be disbursed by the High Court in favour
of the respondent-complainant at the time of passing the
final order.
10. With the aforesaid, the Special Leave Petition stands
disposed of.
11. Pending  application(s),  if  any,  shall  also  stand
disposed of.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL ORIGINAL JURISDICTION
Transfer Petition(Civil)  No.1820/2025
MEGHA TALWAR                                       Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
CHIRAG TANDON                                      Respondent(s)
O R D E R
1. The matter was taken up today for further hearing in the
Committee Room.
2. The petitioner is personally present along with her parents.
3. The Respondent - Chirag Tandon is also personally present. The
learned counsel appearing for the parties are also before us.
4. Our last Order dated 27-2-2026 reads thus:-
   1. Our order dated 2.2.2026, we passed the following order:-
"1. The parties are personally present in the Court today. 
2. The parties are highly educated. Petitioner is serving
in a Multinational Company whereas the husband is a Doctor.
3. There are no issues born in the wedlock.
4. The parties are still not sure whether to put an end to
their marriage or try to save the marriage. After talking
in brief with both, we are of the view that they should
talk for one last time with each other and come back after
two weeks before this Court. If they are able to arrive at
an amicable settlement on their own, nothing like that. All
that is required is some mutual understanding and respect
for each other. If they want to save the marriage and
proceed further, they need to forget the past and bury
their differences.
5. We urged both the parties to meet, talk and try to find
a way out. If they are not able to find a way-out, we shall
proceed to hear this mater further.
6. Post it on 26-2-2026 at 3.30 p.m. in the Committee
Room.”

## Page 399

2
2. In pursuance of our aforesaid order, the parties are present
before us. We first had a talk with the petitioner, Megha Talwar,
who is personally present along with her parents.
3. Thereafter, we had a talk with the respondent, Chirag Tandon.
4. After talking to the parties, we have reached the conclusion that
this is a case of irretrievable breakdown of marriage.
5. The parties are also sure that it will be next to impossible to
live a happy marital life. Both have decided to part ways by
getting the marriage dissolved.
6. The parties have reached to a consensus that the respondent
husband Chirag Tandon shall pay an amount of Rs.75,00,000/- (Rupees
Seventy Five lakh only) towards full and final settlement.
7. In view of the aforesaid, we now want the parties to reduce the
settlement into writing and place it before us.
8. It is understood that the marriage will be dissolved and all
litigation(s) between the parties, civil and criminal, shall stand
terminated.
9. The respondent makes a statement that he shall make the payment
of Rs.75,00,000/- (Rs.Seventy Five lakh only) by way of demand draft
in the name of Megha Talwar on or before 13.5.2026. The day the
amount is paid to the petitioner wife, we shall proceed to pass
further orders.
10. We are informed that the petitioner has some of her clothes at
the residence of the respondent. The respondent has undertaken to
hand over all the clothes of the petitioner at the earliest. It is
for the respondent to make the necessary arrangements to deliver the
clothes to the petitioner.
11. Post this matter on 13.5.2026 at 3.00 P.M. in the Committee
Room.”
5. In pursuance of our last Order dated February 27, 2026, the
parties have been able to reach to an amicable settlement.
6. The Settlement Agreement has been reduced into writing duly
signed by the parties and their respective counsel.
7. The original Settlement Agreement dated May 13, 2026, is
ordered to be taken on record and shall be kept with the records of
this case. 
8. The parties are directed to abide by all the terms and
conditions of the settlement.

## Page 400

3
9. In accordance with the Agreement, Mr. Chirag (husband)  has
agreed to pay a total sum of Rs.75,00,000/- (Rupees Seventy Five
lakh) to his wife (Megha)  towards full and final settlement.
10 Chirag  has  brought  a  Demand  Draft  of  the  amount  of
Rs.75,00,000/- drawn in favor of Megha. The demand draft  is being
handed over to Megha.
11. The xerox copy of the demand draft is also attached with the
Settlement Agreement. 
12. In view of the aforesaid, all proceedings pending between the
parties, civil and criminal, stand terminated.
13. We dissolve the marriage between the parties in exercise of
our jurisdiction under Article 142 of the Constitution.
14. The Registry to draw a decree accordingly.
15. With the aforesaid, the petition stands disposed of, 
16. Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO(S).          OF 2026  
(Arising out of SLP(Crl.) No(s).  3783/2026)
SHIJI                                APPELLANT(S)
                                VERSUS
GOPINATHA PILLAI & ANR.                     RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. Heard learned counsel for the appellant. 
3. The present appeal, calls in question the correctness  of
the  impugned  judgment/order  dated  14-10-2025  in  CRLA
No.1806/2023 passed by the High Court of Kerala at Ernakulam.
By the said judgment/order, the High Court has reversed the
order of acquittal of the appellant passed by the Judicial
Magistrate  First  Class,  Court-I,  Mavelikkara,  Kerala  (for
short, ‘Trial Court’) and convicted him under Section 138 of
the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (for short, ‘NI Act’) and
sentenced him to imprisonment till the rising of the Court,
apart from the sentence of fine of Rs.1,50,000/- payable within
a period of three months from the date of receipt of the copy
of the High Court judgment/order. In case of default, it was

## Page 403

2
directed  that  the  appellant  shall  undergo  sentence  of
imprisonment of six months. 
4. Being aggrieved, the appellant is before us.
5. The appellant has been exempted from surrendering by the
order of the Hon’ble Chamber Judge dated 13.02.2026 and the
same was extended by this Court’s orders dated 20.02.2026 and
20.04.2026.
6. The respondents, though served, have chose not to appear.
However, we have before us a settlement dated 22.06.2026 which
the appellant has entered into with the respondent no.1. Under
the said settlement, the dispute has been settled for a sum of
Rs.1,25,000/-.
7. Under the settlement, the amount of Rs.75,000/-, lying in
the Court of Judicial Magistrate First Class, Mavelikkara,
pursuant to the directions of this Court passed on 20.02.2026,
would be withdrawn by the respondent no.1. Additionally, a sum
of Rs.50,000/- has been paid by the appellant on 07.08.2026 to
the respondent no.1. Appropriate receipt is also filed before
us.
8. We are satisfied that the offence has been compounded.
The compounding will have the effect of acquittal of the
appellant.
9. Therefore, in view of the said settlement, the impugned
judgment/order dated 14.10.2025 is set aside.
10. The appeal is disposed of in the above terms.

2. The contention in the above case is only of limitation under 
Chapter XXXVI of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 1. An FIR 
No.470 of 2018 dated 22.04.2018 was registered pursuant to a 
motor vehicle accident. The offences alleged were under Sections 
279, 337 and 304A of Indian Penal Code 2. The charge -sheet was 
filed on 15.03.2022 produced as Annexure P2; beyond the three 
year period.  The offence s alleged are punishable with 
imprisonment of 6 months to 2 years respectively. 
 
1 For brevity, ‘the Cr.P.C’ 
2 For brevity, ‘the IPC’ 

## Page 407

Page 2 of 2 
3. Section 468 of the Cr.P.C. bars cognizance after one year; 
with respect to offences punishable with imprisonment for a term 
not exceeding one year and three years, with respect to offences 
punishable with imprisonment for a term exceeding one year but 
not exceeding three years. The charge-sheet has been filed after 
three years and no cognizance can be taken in the nature of the 
rigor of the limitation provided under Cr.P.C. 
4. We hence quash the charge-sheet and allow the appeal. 
5. The appellant shall stand discharged.  
6. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

1. Leave granted.
2. Appellants are the father in law and
mother in law of the deceased,  Damini  Sahu ,
who committed suicide at her matrimonial home
on 02.04.2022. This led to lodging of the FIR
against the appellants and their son, Jitesh
Sahu.  All the three were sent for trial and
have been convicted for committing offence
under Sections 304 read with 34 of the Indian
Penal Code, 1860.
3. Under the impugned order, the High Court
has refused to allow the appellants’ prayer
for suspension of sentence and rejected the
their prayer for release on bail.

## Page 411

2
4. The appellant no.1, Pawan Kumar Sahu , is
the father in law and appellant no.2, Padmani
Sahu, is the mother in law of the deceased,
Damini Sahu.
5. Having  considered  the  nature  of
allegations against the appellants and for the
fact  that  the  appellants  have  suffered
incarceration for about one year and 10 months
and the main allegation is against the husband
of the deceased, we are inclined to allow the
appeal.
6. Accordingly, the appeal stands allowed.
The impugned order passed by the High Court is
set aside and the sentence imposed upon the
appellants shall remain suspended during the
pendency of the appeal, and they are directed
to be released on bail upon such terms and
conditions as may be imposed by the Trial
Court,.
7. However,  appellants  shall  continue  to
cooperate with the hearing of the appeal as
and when it is taken up for consideration by
the High Court.

                   Dr. Vijay Kumar Sharma, Adv.
                                      
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. In terms of the orders dated 13.08.1998 and 06.10.1999, t hese
appeals/petitions,  which  raise  the  question  of  legislative
competence of a State Legislature to levy an additional surcharge
calculated on sales tax payable by a dealer, have been referred to
a Bench of Seven Judges.
2

## Page 432

2. The reference was prompted by the conflicting views taken by a
five Judge Bench in S. Kodar v. State of Kerala, 1975(1) SCR 121
and a Three Judge Bench in Hoechst Pharmaceuticals Ltd. v. State of
Bihar and others , 1983(4) SCC 45. There also seems to be some
degree of conflict with some observations made by a Seven Judge
Bench in India Cements Ltd. and others  v. State of Tamil Nadu and
others, 1990 (1) SCC 12.
3. In  this  context,  a  Bench  of  Seven  Judges  ought  to  be
constituted to hear this matter and adjudicate the following
question of law:
(i) Whether  the  imposition  of  a  surcharge/additional
tax/levy/cess/sale/purchase, which is calculated on the basis of a
validly levied sales/purchase tax, is beyond the competence of the
State Legislature?
(ii) Any other issue(s) that may arise during the course of
hearing.
4. This Court had, vide order dated 09.01.2024, appointed Ms.
Anindita Pujari as nodal counsel with a direction to compile a
common  compilation  of  submissions,  pleadings,  documents,  and
precedents, and to have written submissions made in electronic form
and sent to this Court by 02.04.2024. A substantial part of the
case management required for the hearing of these appeals has thus
been completed.
5. In the intervening period, Ms. Anindita Pujari has been
designated as a Senior Advocate. Consequently, on the suggestion of
3

## Page 433

the learned Senior Counsel/counsel for the parties, we appoint Ms.
Samapika Biswal (samapikabiswal91@gmail.com) as the nodal counsel.
6. Accordingly, we grant liberty to the parties to update their
written  submissions  or  submit  fresh  written  submissions  by
15.09.2026. In this regard, the nodal counsel may provide her
assistance and facilitate submissions before the Bench by putting
together  fresh  common  compilation  of  submissions,  pleadings,
documents, and precedents.
7. We propose that the matter be heard by the Bench of Seven
Judges only post-lunch from 2:00 PM onwards. The hearing will
commence on 22.09.2026 and is expected to conclude by 24.09.2026. 
8. Keeping this schedule in mind, the learned nodal counsel may
accordingly coordinate with the arguing counsel for allocation of
the timeline. It goes without saying that the time schedule shall
be  strictly  followed,  and  learned  counsel  will  endeavour  to
complete their arguments within the time allotted.

1. Leave granted.

3. Impugned order of the High Court dated 26.03.2026 reads as
follows:
1. This petition has been filed challenging
an  order  dated  28.10.2022  passed  by  Sub
Divisional Magistrate, Handia, Prayagraj.
2. The petition is badly barred by laches
which  has  not  been  explained  and  is
accordingly, dismissed.
4. On 23.06.2026, we had passed the following order:
1. The writ petition of the petitioner was
dismissed on the ground of laches.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits
that  there  was  prolonged  illness  of
petitioner’s mother and eventually she passed
away. Therefore, there was some delay in
filing the writ petition assailing the order
dated 28.10.2022. In any view of the matter,
she  submits  that  there  is  no  period  of
limitation prescribed as such insofar writ
jurisdiction  is  concerned.  Further,  the
1

impugned  order  is  wholly  a  non  speaking
order.
2. Issue notice, returnable on 27.07.2026.

for the petitioner to serve notice upon the
Standing counsel for the respondent-State of
Uttar Pradesh.
4. In the meantime, status quo as on today as
regards the property in question shall be
maintained.
5. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and on due
consideration, we are of the view that the Writ Petition filed by
the appellant should be heard on merits. 
6. Learned State counsel submits that he has no objection to
this.
7. In view of the above, we set aside the impugned order of the
High Court dated 26.03.2026 and remand the matter back to the High
Court for hearing and deciding Writ (C) No.9232/2026 on its own
merit. The status  quo order passed by this Court shall continue
till disposal of the writ petition by the High Court.
8. Appeal is accordingly allowed.

1. The grievance of the petitioner is that against
the order of the learned Single Judge of the High
Court  dated  16.02.2023  passed  in  Writ-A  No.
1450/2023, Special Appeal No. 133/2023 has been filed
before Division Bench of the High Court which is
pending  consideration  and  the  prayer  for  interim
protection has not yet been decided in the pending
Special  Appeal  and,  in  the  meantime,  contempt
1

## Page 484

proceedings have been initiated and by the impugned
order, date has been fixed for framing charges.
2. It is the case of the petitioner that if the
order of the learned Single Judge is implemented
without giving opportunity to the petitioner to press
the stay application in the pending Special Appeal,
grave injustice would be done.
3. We find it quite strange that the Special Appeal
No. 133/2023 filed in 2023 is yet not taken up for
consideration of stay application. It is possible
that the petitioner himself may be guilty of taking
adjournment but we do not wish to express any opinion
on that.
4. Having regard to the peculiar facts of the case,
we deem it appropriate to dispose of this petition by
requesting the High Court to ensure that the stay
application/Special Appeal No. 133/2023 filed by the
petitioner be accorded consideration within two weeks
from the date of filing of an application before the
concerned Bench of the High Court along with a copy
of this order.
5. To enable presentation of such application, for
a period of one week from today, bailable warrants
issued to the petitioner shall remain in abeyance.
6. If within the aforesaid period, the application
is presented before the concerned Bench of the High
Court  for  consideration  of  the  stay  application/
2

## Page 485

Special Appeal No.133/2023, the interim protection
granted above shall continue for a further period of
two weeks till the aforesaid application is addressed
by the concerned Bench of the High Court.
7. The Special Leave Petition stands disposed of in
the aforesaid terms.
8. We make it clear that we have not expressed
opinion  on  the  merits  of  the  aforesaid  Special
Appeal. 
9. Pending  application(s),  if  any,  shall  stand
disposed of.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Heard Mr. Babul Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioner
-wife and Mr. Ravindra Sadanand Chingale, learned counsel for
the respondent-husband. 
2. We also interacted with Ms. Madhavi Krishna-wife and
Mr.Bharat Kumar Irranki-husband through video conferencing.

## Page 526

2
Both the husband and wife are very reasonable and practical in
their approach. We are of the opinion that with a little bit
of effort, the whole matter can be amicably resolved. We are
also anxious that two girl children, aged approximately 10
years and 8 years, should be the utmost priority. 
3. Keeping in mind the above fact, we record the statement
of  husband-Bharat  Kumar  Irranki,  that  he  is  willing  to
facilitate a one to one interaction on exclusive basis between
wife-Madhavi Krishna and the two children, who were now in the
custody  of  father.  As  and  when  wife  desires  to  visit
Hyderabad, the husband will facilitate the said interaction.
The husband has a submission that last time when his wife
visited there, the children are unwilling for a one to one
interaction. 
4. We suggest that father-Bharat Kumar Irranki advices the
children to interact with the mother, keeping their larger
interest in mind. 
5. Further, without prejudice the rights and contentions of
the  parties,  the  husband  will  also  transfer  a  sum  of
Rs.50,000/- directly in the account of his wife within a
period of three weeks from today.
6. Parties to coordinate about the visits. 

## Page 527

3
7. In the meantime, the phone calls and video calls shall
continue between the mother and the children. 
8. Post the matters on 18th November, 2026.
9. Liberty to mention.

1. Heard  Ms. Nandita Rao, learned Senior Counsel for the
petitioner. Learned Senior Counsel submits that Section 37
appeal of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (for
short, ‘A&C Act’) itself was filed against the order of Civil
Judge (Junior Division), Gurugram, Haryana(for short, ‘Civil
Judge, Gurugram’). The Civil Judge, Gurugram, had dismissed
the Section 8 Application of  A&C Act, primarily relying on
the observations of the High Court of Punjab & Haryana at
Chanidgarh in C.R.No.5780/2025 under which the order setting

## Page 553

2
the petitioner ex-parte in the suit was set aside.
2. The contention of the learned Senior Counsel is that
Section 8 of A&C Act is that the Civil Judge, Gurugram erred
in dismissing the application by relying on the observations
of the High Court” which according to learned Senior Counsel
was made in the context of order 9 rule 13 of Code of Civil
Procedure, 1908(for short, ‘CPC’). Learned Senior Counsel
submits that by the impugned order, while the Section 37
appeal of A&C Act, is registered, interim stay of suit has not
been granted.
3. Be that as it may, these are for the Additional District
Judge, Gurugram, Haryana (for short, ‘ADJ, Gurugram’), to
consider while hearing the appeal.
4. We are told that the appeal is posted on 11.09.2026.
5. We also told that the respondent(s) is served in the
appeal.
6. We direct that the appeal be taken up by the ADJ,
Gurugram on 24.08.2026.
7. In  the  meantime,  let  the  Civil  Judge,  Gurugram  be
apprised of this Court’s order. The Civil Judge, Gurugram,
shall postpone the suit to a date, after 24.08.2026. 
8. Needless to say that appeal before the ADJ, Gurugram be
decided  on  its  own  merits,  uninfluenced  by  any  of  the
observations in the present order.
9. With the above observations, the Special Leave Petition
is disposed of.
10. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL NO(s).  507 OF 2015  
THE STATE OF WEST BENGAL & ORS.                    APPELLANT(S)
                                VERSUS
DIPAK SUBBA                                        RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. The appellants challenge the judgment/order dated
08.08.2013 in WPST No.301 of 2013 passed by the High
Court of Calcutta.
2. As  per  the  Office  Report  dated  28.07.2026,
alternative arrangement notice on the sole respondent is
complete, but none has entered appearance, perhaps for
the reason that with the passage of time, the respondent
would have lost interest, since the impugned order dated
08.08.2013 passed in his favour was stayed by this Court
vide order dated 07.10.2013.
3. From the order passed by the Tribunal rejecting the
appellants'  claim,  it  is  evident  that  criminal
proceedings stood initiated against the respondent for
having forged documents, in particular the school leaving
certificate, which formed part of the selection process
for the post of constable. The High Court took the view
that  unless  proven  otherwise,  the  presumption  of
innocence operates in favour of the candidate, and as
1

## Page 556

such, he was entitled to consideration for appointment to
the post of constable.
4. We are of the considered view that the High Court
fell into error, more so when, as has emerged from the
record, a chargesheet stood filed against the respondent,
for having committed the crime, with regard to the very
same  document  based  on  which,  he  was  seeking  his
appointment.
5. In view of the above, the impugned judgment/order
dated 08.08.2013 shall stand set aside.
6. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.
7. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The underlying issue in this batch of petitions concerns
substantial questions of law with respect to the definition of the
breach  or  limits  of  legislative  privileges,  vis-à-vis the
interpretation of Articles 194(3) and 19(1)(a) and their interplay,
along with that of Article 21 and the interpretation of other
provisions of the Constitution.
2. Although these petitions were initially referred to a Bench of
Five Judges vide order dated 08.12.2003, this Court subsequently
identified certain conflicting observations made by a Seven Judge
Bench in Special Reference No.1/1964, (1965) 1 SCR 413, and those
made by a Five Judge Bench in Pandit M.S.M. Sharma  v. Shri Krishna
Sinha, 1959 Supp.(1) SCR 806. Consequently, the matter was placed
before a Bench of Seven Judges for adjudication of the issues
involved.
3. This Court dated 12.03.2023, appointed Ms. Devyani Gupta and
Ms. Purnima Krishna as the nodal counsel with a direction to
compile a common compilation of submissions, pleadings, documents
and precedents, and to have written submissions made in electronic
form and sent to this Court by 21.10.2023. A substantial part of
the case management for hearing of these petitions thus already
stand completed. Meanwhile, Ms. Francesca Samuel, AOR, has been
2

## Page 605

appointed as the standing counsel for the State of Tamil Nadu in
place of Ms. Purnima Krishna.
4. Consequently, Ms. Devyani Gupta and Ms. Francesca Samuel will
continue to be the nodal counsel, who may submit fresh written
submissions on or before 28.09.2026. They will also facilitate a
fresh common compilation of submissions, pleadings, documents and
precedents.
5. The matter shall be listed before a Bench of seven Judges on
06.10.2026, at 11 A.M. The matter is expected to conclude on
15.10.2026.
6. The nodal counsel, in consultation with Senior Counsel/other
arguing counsel, will arrange a time schedule so that the hearing
in the matter can be completed within the allocated time. It goes
without saying that the time schedule shall be strictly followed,
and learned counsel will endeavour to complete their arguments
within the time allotted.
(ARJUN BISHT)                              (PREETHI DILEEP KUMAR)
ASTT. REGISTRAR-cum-PS                        DY. REGISTRAR

only to buttress its conclusion that the appeal,
which is hopelessly barred by time, need not be
entertained.  In  such  circumstances,  those
observations will not have any bearing on the rights
of the parties in the execution proceedings.

leave petition stands disposed of.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. We heard Ms. Swati Mishra, the learned counsel appearing for
the appellant - convict and Mr. Nishant Awana, the learned counsel
appearing for the State.
2. We are of the view that no error, not to speak of any error of
law, could be said to have been committed by the High Court in
dismissing the appeal preferred by the appellant and thereby
affirming the Judgment and Order of conviction passed by the Trial
Court holding the appellant guilty of the offence of murder of his
wife. 
3. We take notice of the fact that the incident is of the year
2011. The appellant has undergone almost more than 14 years of
sentence. In February 2026, this Court while admitting this appeal
ordered his release on bail and since then he is on bail. 

## Page 1071

2
4. We would like to know two things from the jail authorities:-
(i) The overall conduct of the appellant over a period of years;
(ii) His conduct or his movements after he was ordered to be
released on bail by this Court in February 2026. 
5. We would also like to know from the State as regards the
remission policy prevailing as on the date of the commission of the
alleged offence or any other remission policy which may be more
beneficial to the appellant. 
6. Let an appropriate Report come on record by next date of
hearing. 
7. Post it on 11-9-2026 at the end of the Board.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioner, on instructions,
and after consulting the son of the petitioner,  who is present before the Court
would submit that dispute between petitioner and informant lies in a narrow
compass namely relating to an Agreement to Sell dated 23.10.2023 and the
said dispute can be resolved and to show the bona fides  of the petitioner, he
submits that the petitioner is ready and willing to refund the entire amount
reflected in the agreement to sell (Rs. Eight Crore)  if some reasonable time is
granted  and for the purpose of refunding the said amount, he seeks two
months’ time. Placing his submission on record, we direct this matter to be
listed after four weeks and on the said date petitioner shall refund some
reasonable amount out of the total amount agreed to be repaid.
2. In the meanwhile, there shall be interim protection from any
coercive steps being taken against the petitioner and only on account of
aforesaid submission made for refunding the amount this protective order has
been passed.
3. We make it clear if, the petitioner fails to exhibit any bona fides this
order would not be continued.
4. Tag the matter along with SLP (Crl) No. 14484/2026.

                             O R D E R
1. Delay condoned.
2. It is argued that petitioner Amar Singh  was sent on
trial with co-accused  Sunil and  Hanuman for committing
murder of deceased  Surender on 02.03.2000. As per the
deposition  of  eyewitness  PW-10  Rampal,  all  the  three
accused were together at the time of incident, and Sunil
and  Hanuman caught hold of the witness, and the present
petitioner took out a pistol from the pocket of his pant
1

and fired shot at deceased Surender.
3. It is argued that disbelieving the statement of
eyewitness qua Sunil and Hanuman, they have been acquitted
by  the  Trial  Court  and  only  the  petitioner  has  been
convicted.
4. Issue notice, on Special Leave Petition as well as
on bail, returnable in ten weeks.
5. In the meanwhile, record of the trial court be
summoned.
